newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Occidental scales down Colombia output.
newsitem.headline: Occidental scales down Colombia output.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp has scaled back crude output at its Cano Limon field in eastern Colombia to between 70,000 and 80,000 barrels per day, from the daily average of 180,000 barrels, in the wake of a pipeline attack by leftist guerrillas, a company spokesman said Wednesday.

The spokesman said Occidental would decide by "late afternoon" or this evening on whether to shut down production completely until the pipeline, which pumps crude to the Caribbean coast port at Covenas, was repaired.
The pipeline, which has a 300,000 barrels per day capacity, was blown up by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels for the 36th time this year last Sunday.
The rebels later shot down a helicopter carrying troops to the blast site, killing 20 soldiers and one civilian crew member.

A spokesman for the state-run oil company Ecopetrol said repair teams had not yet been able to reach the area because of on-going firefights between the army and guerrillas. He said he hoped the teams would arrive at the point where the pipeline was blown up, near the town of Arauquita, in Arauca province Wednesday afternoon.

"At this moment it's border line whether we will be shutting- in or not. We're producing increasingly less. We're now down to about 70,000 or 80,000 barrels per day. We will know by late afternoon or early evening whether there will be a shut-in," an Occidental spokesman told Reuters.
Occidental has only a small storage capacity at its Cano Limon field, thereby forcing cuts in production if the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline remains out of service for several days at a time.
The Ecopetrol spokesman estimated that production of more than one million barrels of crude from Cano Limon had been lost so far this year because of repeated pipeline attacks.
The ELN, a Cuban-inspired force set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, specializes in attacks on the country's oil infrastructure.
